Lauren —

Thanks — quick initial numbers from this sprint:
- Current quarterly GPU spend (run-rate): ~$2.1M / month (excl. reserved discounts).
- Utilization (pooled inference clusters): 68% overall; tail 90th percentile latency-friendly pool at 82%.
- Batching experiment (adaptive batch size): reduced per-token CPU overhead, estimated 12% token-cost reduction on batch-friendly jobs.

Notes: we pushed a 4-bit quantization candidate to one canary pool (Llama-variant) — shows no visible quality regression in the narrow eval set; estimated additional ~8% cost savings for those model classes once promoted.

I've attached batching_experiment_results.csv with raw traces and a short readme line. Will follow up with a slide summarizing methodology.

-Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Lauren / Markus —

Adding the unit-econ delta worksheet and a short summary of assumptions (see attached unit_econ_deltas.xlsx):
- Baseline: $2.10M/mo GPU run-rate -> blended cost per 1k tokens = $0.0132 (inference-heavy mix).
- With adaptive batching + better slot packing: projected blended cost/1k = $0.0116 (~12% improvement for batchable traffic).
- With selective prefix/KV caching on streaming (50% of prefix reuse): additional ~9% improvement for those routes; end-to-end savings depend on routing mix.
- Combined: realistic near-term improvement window = 18–20% on token spend for workloads that are both batchable and cache-friendly.

Operational impact:
- Expected utilization increase by 4–6 percentage points as we pack more short jobs into batches.
- Risk: latency-sensitive tail can degrade if we over-batch; we recommend per-route SLOs and dynamic batch caps.

I've added a short note in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QbrPrepCapacity — slides + the raw traces. I'll highlight the per-model breakdown for the QBR slide (small table showing model-class, baseline cost, savings).

-Vivek
Head of Infra Economics
Redwood Inference
